when: pip3 install -r requirements.txt → "Could not open requirements file: No such file or directory" and make build → "No rule to make target 'build'", right after cloning or when the shell cwd is a workspace rather than the repo
action: Before running install or build commands, locate the real project root instead of assuming cwd: `find <workspace> -maxdepth 6 \( -name pyproject.toml -o -name setup.py -o -name requirements.txt -o -name Makefile \) -not -path '*/node_modules/*'`. Then use the absolute path to that root for every command (pip install -r "$R/requirements.txt", cd "$R" && make ...). Check Makefile targets with `grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:' Makefile` before calling `make build`, since many repos don't define one. Use `pip install "$R"` for the local package.

when: find /usr/lib -name 'libta_lib*' returns nothing and ldconfig -p | grep ta_lib is empty after building a C library, so the Python binding's build or import can't find the native lib
action: Native C libraries often use hyphens, not underscores (e.g. libta-lib.so, not libta_lib.so). Search with both spellings and with a loose pattern: `ls -l /usr/lib/libta-lib* /usr/local/lib/libta-lib* 2>/dev/null; ldconfig -p | grep -i ta-lib`. Confirm the library is registered with ldconfig and that --prefix matches where it was installed before pip-installing the Python binding. Don't chain the ldconfig step with && after a find that may return nothing; a nonzero exit hides the real result.
